Venn Diagram - Twill Derivatives
Twill is the second basic weave in the order of Plain, Twill and Sateen. There are many twill derivatives out of which wavy twill (also called Pointed twill) and diamond are the common one. Wavy twill is again of two kinds; one is wavy twill along and other is wavy twill across. In a loom it is possible to produce all the said four weaves that is twill, wavy twill along, wavy twill across and diamond combinedly. The venn diagram explains about the two different drafts - straight & reverse (Pointed) and two different treadling order (peg-plan) - straight & reverse (Pointed) to be followed to weave in the loom
